```{r loaddata, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyr)
library(lubridate)
logged_data <- read.csv("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSmUPLB7jL4d00cEHQSpFoTLtxfo3ZRLe1480bfGlNWeD8Kydc1Iq17xGcqw2asaD5FViJUz545cV33/pub?output=csv") %>%
  rename(
    Platform       = 2,
    Ads_Seen       = 3,
    Ads_Interacted = 4,
    Ads_Relevant   = 5,
    Ad_Repeated    = 6
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Timestamp         = dmy_hms(Timestamp),
    Date              = as_date(Timestamp),
    Hour              = hour(Timestamp),
    Week              = week(Timestamp),
    Platform_clean    = str_to_title(str_trim(Platform)),
    Is_Video_Platform = str_detect(Platform_clean, "TikTok|Instagram|YouTube"),
    Interaction_Rate  = Ads_Interacted / Ads_Seen
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Ads_Seen))

platform_summary <- logged_data %>%
  group_by(Platform_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    Avg_Ads_Seen         = mean(Ads_Seen, na.rm = TRUE),
    Avg_Ads_Interacted   = mean(Ads_Interacted, na.rm = TRUE),
    Avg_Interaction_Rate = mean(Interaction_Rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    Sessions             = n()
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Avg_Ads_Seen))

daily_summary <- logged_data %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Ads_Seen       = sum(Ads_Seen, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Ads_Interacted = sum(Ads_Interacted, na.rm = TRUE),
    Sessions             = n(),
    Avg_Ads_Seen         = Total_Ads_Seen / Sessions
  )

daily_summary_filled <- daily_summary %>%
  complete(Date = seq(min(Date), max(Date), by = "day"))

my_colours <- c("#E5CEeC","#C83184","#F0F0F0","#AA4479","#982649","#6A041D","black","white")

my_theme <- theme(
  plot.background  = element_rect(fill = my_colours[1]),
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = my_colours[1]),
  panel.grid       = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
  axis.line        = element_blank(),
  plot.margin      = margin(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, "cm"),
  plot.title       = element_text(colour = my_colours[6])
)
```

      }

  });
})

## Introduction

Over several weeks, I logged my social media usage across 20-minute phone sessions, recording how many ads I encountered, how many I interacted with, whether they felt relevant, and whether any repeated. This story explores what the data reveals about the nature of advertising across social media platforms.

## Which Platform Shows the Most Ads?

Not all social media platforms deliver the same advertising experience.
The chart below shows the average number of ads seen per 20-minute session on each platform.

```{r plot1, fig.alt="Bar chart showing average number of ads seen per social media platform per 20-minute session"}

ggplot(platform_summary, aes(x = reorder(Platform_clean, Avg_Ads_Seen),
                               y = Avg_Ads_Seen,
                               fill = Platform_clean)) +
    geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(Avg_Ads_Seen, 1)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5,
              colour = my_colours[6]) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(my_colours[2], my_colours[3], my_colours[4],
                                 my_colours[5], my_colours[6])) +
    labs(
      title    = "Average Number of Ads Seen per Social Media Platform",
      subtitle = "Based on 20-minute phone use sessions",
      x        = "Platform",
      y        = "Average Ads Seen",
      caption  = "Source: Personal logged data"
    ) +
    my_theme
```

This plot revels that facebook has the highest number of ads recorded within a 20 minute period, with an average of 26.6 ads, whereas youtube has the lowest number of recorded ads with an average of 0.1 ads within a 20 minute session. 

## Do I Actually Engage With the Ads I See?

Seeing an ad and interacting with it are very different things. The scatter plot below shows the relationship between how many ads I saw and how many I interacted with across all sessions.

```{r plot2, fig.alt="Scatter plot showing relationship between ads seen and ads interacted with, coloured by platform"}
ggplot(logged_data, aes(x = Ads_Seen, y = Ads_Interacted, colour = Platform_clean)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = my_colours[7], linetype = "solid") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(my_colours[2], my_colours[3], my_colours[4],
                                 my_colours[5], my_colours[6])) +
  labs(
    title    = "Relationship Between Ads Seen and Ads Interacted With",
    subtitle = "Each point represents one 20-minute session",
    x        = "Number of Ads Seen",
    y        = "Number of Ads Interacted With",
    colour   = "Platform",
    caption  = "Source: Personal logged data"
  ) +
  my_theme
```

Despite the graph looking linear in a positive direction, my interaction rate remained consistently low, even with a large number of ads seen, suggesting that most ads, regardless of platform, did not feel compelling enough to engage with.

## How Did My Ad Exposure Change Over Time?

Finally, looking at how ad exposure changed across the logging period reveals interesting patterns in my phone usage habits

```{r plot3, fig.alt="Line chart showing average ads seen per day over the logging period from March to May 2026"}
ggplot(daily_summary, aes(x = Date, y = Avg_Ads_Seen)) +
  geom_line(colour = my_colours[5], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(colour = my_colours[6], size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%d %b", date_breaks = "2 days") +
  labs(
    title    = "Average Ads Seen Per Day Over the Logging Period",
    subtitle = "Average across all 20-minute sessions per day",
    x        = "Date",
    y        = "Average Ads Seen per Session",
    caption  = "Source: Personal logged data | Timestamp parsed with {lubridate}"
  ) +
  my_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, colour = my_colours[6]))

```

Ad exposure was higher during certain weeks, possibly reflecting increased phone usage during busier or more stressful periods. The gaps in the data reflect days where no logging sessions were recorded.

## Conclusion

This personal data story highlights how advertising is deeply embedded in everyday social media use. Even within short 20-minute sessions, users are exposed to a significant number of ads most of which go unnoticed or unengaged with. Additionally Each visualisation was built using {ggplot2}, mapping variables to aesthetic properties such as position, colour, and size, following the grammar of graphics framework.
